name: Brusselator chemical oscillator
description:
Prigogine and Lefever's model of an autocatalytic reaction, the Brusselator. A feeds X; X turns into Y at rate B·X; two X and a Y make three X, at rate X²·Y; and X leaves at rate X. With A and B held at 1 and 3, each of those steps is a source or a transfer on the diagram, and together they make dX/dt = A + X²Y − (B + 1)X and dY/dt = BX − X²Y.

The steady state (A, B/A) = (1, 3) is unstable whenever B > 1 + A², so instead of settling the concentrations run round a limit cycle, X spiking every 7.15 seconds.

Try: B = 1.5. Below the threshold the oscillations die away, into the steady state (1, 1.5).
